title: Get the Maximum Score
summary: Given two sorted arrays of distinct integers, determine the maximum score by choosing a path that allows switching between the arrays at a single repeated value.
statement: Given two sorted arrays of distinct integers, determine the maximum score by choosing a path that allows switching between the arrays at a single repeated value. The score is the sum of unique values in the path, modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Both arrays are strictly increasing and positive; traverse either array from left to right and may switch at shared values.
Count a shared value once and return the maximum path sum modulo 1,000,000,007.
reference_solution:
def maximum_two_array_path_score(nums1, nums2):
 i=j=0;left=right=0
 while i<len(nums1) and j<len(nums2):
  if nums1[i]<nums2[j]:left+=nums1[i];i+=1
  elif nums2[j]<nums1[i]:right+=nums2[j];j+=1
  else:left=right=max(left,right)+nums1[i];i+=1;j+=1
 left+=sum(nums1[i:]);right+=sum(nums2[j:])
 return max(left,right)%1000000007

def maximum_two_array_path_score(nums1, nums2):
 i=j=0;left=right=0
 while i<len(nums1) and j<len(nums2):
  if nums1[i]<nums2[j]:left+=nums1[i];i+=1
  elif nums2[j]<nums1[i]:right+=nums2[j];j+=1
  else:left=right=max(left,right)+nums1[i]*2;i+=1;j+=1
 left+=sum(nums1[i:]);right+=sum(nums2[j:])
 return max(left,right)%1000000007
hints: Accumulate segment sums independently while advancing two pointers.
At a shared value, both paths can arrive there, so set both totals to the larger prior total plus that value once.
After the final crossing, append each remaining tail and take the larger total.
Any switch is possible only at a shared value, making each between-crossing segment an independent maximum choice.
